purpose: Teach: よら/云っ/よろしけれ/ぶち/つぶれ/とどまら/創る/ココロ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんに何にもよらない用事があった
lines.en: Your grandfather, when he was young — he never needed much reason to come visit us.
lines.style: Soft, remembering tone. Long pause before the dash. Gentle nostalgia without melancholy. Voice settling into the past tense. Slow, deliberate pacing — not rushing the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、「お疲れ」と云って下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm, yes — he'd say "I'm tired" to your father and just sit with us, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Bright recognition. Quick, intimate. Leans into the shared memory. Slight conspiratorial warmth. The "dear?" at the end is a gentle check — is he remembering the same thing? Affectionate.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「よろしければ」と丁寧に仰った
lines.en: When he was young, your grandfather would say things so carefully — "If you don't mind" — so polite.
lines.style: Thoughtful pause at the opening. Voice settling deeper into admiration. The quoted phrase delivered with almost-tender precision. Slow exhale after. Not criticising politeness — praising it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、悔しい時は「ぶち壊し」と仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather — when he got frustrated in those days, he'd say "I'm going to break it all" — but he never really did, did he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle tease under warmth. Quick on the dialogue. A small, knowing laugh hiding in the words. The "did he, dear?" asks for confirmation of a story she treasures. Intimate, testing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、村のお店がつぶれてしまった事があった
lines.en: Back then, the village shop your father was thinking of opening — it failed before it even started.
lines.style: Steady, factual opening. Slight pain underneath, not performed. Matter-of-fact about hardship. Trails a little at the end — the weight of that disappointment hanging there. Still wistful, not bitter.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、現状にとどまらない冒険心がおありだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: But he didn't stay stuck there, did he? Your grandfather had that restless courage in him — always looking forward.
lines.style: Warm observation. The "didn't he?" is a gentle prompt for agreement. Slight lift on "restless courage" — pride in him. Slow, sure pacing. Not glossing over the pain, but pointing past it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが家庭を創る事に責任を持ってらした
lines.en: When he was young, he took responsibility seriously — for the home he was building, for all of us.
lines.style: Reverent, measured. Slight emphasis on "responsibility." Deep, grounded tone. Not urgent. The kind of thing said once, meant forever. Quiet strength in the voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様の「ココロ」を理解されてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he understood — your grandchildren's hearts — he really understood us, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Soft, almost wondering. The hesitation before "hearts" — reaching for the right word, finding it. Tender, close, intimate. Voice very quiet on the final "didn't he, dear?" — asking him to confirm something sacred.
